sites: $.purpose — 'deciding the cancellation dual-carrier tension D-015 routed here.'

measurement.what those 4 lines are: 251 = D-001 decided-class list; 461 = touched-classes list; 830/844 = D-007 manifest/DR-125 capability dual boundary. None routes T-1.
measurement.pinned-blob control: D-015 is BYTE-IDENTICAL between the artifact's own pinned blob 12d192f (commit 2327cf8) and live HEAD; diff since the pin is 188 insertions / 0 deletions. 'T-1' count in the pinned blob is also 0.

blockers.why: D-015's actual content records control-protocol-contract.v2 as DR-102's accepted design contract and states 'No freeze or claim-register motion; no pins move'. Its single routing act is a correction dropping DR-G15 in favour of DR-120/DR-G21 for conformance fixtures. It routes nothing to DR-125 and never mentions cancellation. The artifact's own pinned evidence refutes the citation, so this is not pin staleness - it is a claim that was never true at any recorded state.
blockers.loadBearing: This is not decorative. The routing is the stated ground on which the artifact REJECTS the alternative 'leave T-1 reported' - the exact disposition CPC v2 reserved. Remove the false routing and the rejection has no recorded basis.
blockers.fix: Delete the three D-015 routing claims, or replace them with a real recorded act. If the coordinator intends DR-125 to own the T-1 composition, that routing must be minted as its own D-000-reviewed decision first; a candidate cannot cite a routing into existence.

blockers.title: Authority escape: a coordinator-reserved disposition converted into a candidate-made decision
sites: $.recordedInputs.governingSources[1].role — 'This artifact is the named owner of the composition decision.'
$.t1CancellationComposition.decision — 'ACCEPT the control-protocol v2 split as the intended reading of file 02.'

measurement.CPC v2 tensionsObserved.discipline: 'Reported, not resolved - per the authoring task. ... none is settled by this artifact.'
measurement.CPC v2 T-1 pendingResolutionThisCandidat: 'Whether that split is the intended reading of file 02 is for the coordinator/reviewer to decide.'

blockers.why: Nothing names DR-125 as the owner of this composition - not CPC v2, not its accepted verdict, not COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, not file 02, not the DR-125 row. CPC v2 expressly reserved the question to the coordinator/reviewer. A T2-02 candidate is neither. The question reserved is which reading of file 02's control-plane demarcation is intended - DR-102 territory, and DR-102's row is already SATISFIED. DR-125's row legitimately covers cancellation INTEGRATION for components; it does not carry authority to settle the protocol-demarcation reading behind it. Deciding it here is precisely the 'authority escape' the DR-125 row's own acceptance column forbids.
blockers.note: The decision's SUBSTANCE is not what is wrong: the supervision/in-band split matches CPC v2 and contradicts no source. What is wrong is the status upgrade from 'reserved for the coordinator' to 'decided by this candidate', and the false 'named owner' basis for it.
blockers.fix: Downgrade to a recommendation addressed to the coordinator (e.g. recommendedDisposition), leaving T-1 formally open; or obtain a recorded routing act first (see B-1). Either restores the artifact to candidate standing without losing the analysis.

shouldFix.title: 'Rule-governed' necessity rests on a must-not verb that file 02's must-not list does not contain
shouldFix.claim: 'File 02's must-not list forbids the control plane from authoring semantic frames of an existing provider protocol.' ... 'The only composition that satisfies both constraints is the supervision/in-band split.'

measurement.file 02 lines 164-165 verbatim: It must not wrap, translate, normalize, reorder, reinterpret, merge, or assign new fates to semantic frames of an existing provider protocol.

shouldFix.why: Every listed verb operates on an EXISTING provider frame. Originating a fresh Cancel frame is not literally any of them, so the cited clause does not by itself yield the claimed uniqueness ('the only composition'). A real prohibition does exist - CPC v2's nonTranslationObligation ('The control plane never closes, drains-to-null, or edits the data plane mid-stream') plus file 02's closed permitted-function list and opacity rule - but that is not the text cited. Labelling the decision RULE-GOVERNED on a misquoted rule asserts the character rather than demonstrating it.
shouldFix.fairness: CPC v2 uses the same 'authoring semantic frames (must-not list)' shorthand, so the artifact inherited it rather than inventing it. The conclusion survives on the correct grounds; only the citation needs repair.
shouldFix.fix: Cite the permitted-function closure plus CPC v2's non-translation obligation, or restate the prohibition in file 02's actual verbs.

summary: The carried text is impeccable - row-verbatim and the 19-line file 02 carry are byte-exact, and every deferral (DR-007, DR-102, DR-108, DR-114, DR-122, DR-105, DR-G20) checks out. The defect is concentrated in the one thing the artifact adds: the T-1 decision. It asserts three times that D-015 routed the composition to DR-125, and D-015 says no such thing in the artifact's own pinned blob - 'T-1' appears zero times in the entire decisions file. On that non-existent mandate it rejects the disposition CPC v2 expressly reserved to the coordinator and settles a reading of file 02's protocol demarcation belonging to DR-102, a row already SATISFIED. The split it lands on is substantively right; the authority to land it is manufactured. Both blockers are fixable without touching the analysis.
